messages:
michelle: Quick follow-up on the continuous-batching RFC — we left headroom slot semantics open for multi-tenant pools. Do we treat headroom as discrete slots or as fractional borrowable capacity? Need to decide for deterministic latency SLOs.

sam: I lean discrete slots + fractional borrowing on top. Guarantees for latency are easier with discrete units, borrow lets us keep utilization up.

ada: :thinking_face: discrete slots worry me for tiny requests (1-2 tokens) — fragmentation could blow throughput. What about slot-slicing (time-sliced slots) so small requests can share a slice?

jorge: Time-slicing helps throughput but makes ordering and KV cache locality non-deterministic. For prefix/KV cache pinning we rely on fairly stable ownership; slicing could increase cache churn.

lee: Proposed config sketch we discussed earlier:
```yaml
scheduler:
  headroom_slots: 2        # discrete reserved slots per tenant
  max_borrow_pct: 0.25     # fraction of other tenants' idle slots allowed to borrow
  slice_ms: 50             # when slicing mode enabled (time slice length)
  deterministic_tie_breaker: hash(tenant_id)  # simple stable ordering
```

sam: Also add an admission hint in the request envelope for latency-sensitive work. Scheduler should prefer giving full discrete slots to `X-Latency-Hint: high`. Example header: `X-Latency-Hint: high|normal|batch`.

michelle: Action items: prototype two modes — (A) discrete slots + borrow (with eviction handshake) and (B) slice mode with stronger eviction. Add a deterministic tie-breaker (tenant hash + sequence) for ordering to keep experiments comparable. @ada can you own prototype A? @lee can you add telemetry (slot_util, borrow_rate, evict_count, kv_pin_churn)?

ada: On it. I'll run a perf job: 1k small requests/s (avg 8 tokens) + 10 large streams. Baseline vs proto-A vs proto-B. ETA EOD Fri.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster started for `headroom-proto-A` — https://k8s.internal/canaries/headroom-proto-A :rocket:

michelle: Nice. Please include a KV-cache pin churn test too — ensure borrowing doesn't cause global thrash. Suggest adding a `kv_pin_ref` counter in the telemetry and a regression alert if churn rate spikes > 2x.

ada: Will add that test and the alert. Also verifying that the eviction handshake includes `kv_cache_keep` hint bit so runtime can try to preserve hot pins where possible.

michelle: Perfect. We'll reconvene after the run to pick the default mode. Thanks everyone.
